text:
Emma L: Heads up — eu-west GPU fleet started flapping after the kernel+driver push around 08:12. Jobs hitting NCCL init failures and p99 token latency spikes. Opening thread to coordinate hotfix/pinning.

Mike T: Seeing same on dedicated pools. Driver rolled to 536.x with CUDA 12.2. Logs show repeated NCCL timeouts and dmesg has lots of `nvidia: GPU watchdog reset` + stack traces. Example from one node:

```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: GPU 0000:81:00: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1234.567891] nvidia 0000:81:00: IRQ 31 for MSI/MSI-X
[ 1234.568000] nccl: Allreduce timeout on comm 0x7f9e7c
```

Priya S: Canary nodes show the regression too — can we pin/hold the driver and CUDA immediately and rollback any nodes that have the new driver? This needs to be fast (customer-facing jobs are impacted).

deploy-bot: deploy failed: rollout gpu-driver-upgrade eu-west: task 23/120 failed -> rollback triggered :fire:

Emma L: Immediate plan:
- Put apt holds on driver+cuda packages on all eu-west GPU hosts
- Cordon/taint nodes that already have the bad driver to stop scheduling new GPU workloads
- Start a small rollback to a known-good driver (535.116) + CUDA 12.1 on a canary pool (5 nodes)

Commands to run on host (run via automation/orchestration, DO NOT run manually at scale):

```
# hold packages to prevent accidental upgrade
sudo apt-mark hold nvidia-driver-536 nvidia-kernel-dkms cuda-toolkit-12-2 libcudnn8

# cordon + drain a node in k8s
kubectl cordon gpu-eu-west-11
kubectl drain gpu-eu-west-11 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
```

Mike T: I'll prepare the 535.116 package bundle and a rollback play. We should also ensure matching NCCL version (2.16.x) — mismatch between driver/CUDA/NCCL/kernel looks like the root cause. I'll stage the rollback on the canary pool, run the nccl-test suite and a small model smoke (latency + throughput).

Priya S: I'll push the apt-mark hold via Ansible across eu-west and create an apt preferences pin so apt won't prefer the new repo bits. Also adding a k8s node label `gpu.upgrade=blocked` while we triage.

Priya S: apt pin snippet I'll apply via config management:

```
# /etc/apt/preferences.d/nvidia-pin
Package: nvidia-*
Pin: version 535.*
Pin-Priority: 700
```

Mike T: Long-term we need a strict lockstep compatibility matrix (driver -> CUDA -> NCCL -> kernel) and enforce it in the orchestration pipeline. No driver upgrades should go wide without: canary success, kernel ABI checks, and a smoke test gate. Propose auto-rollback if canary smoke fails.

sre-oncall: Quick question on impact & timeline: how long do we hold upgrades? Holding forever costs us security updates. We should document a 72-hour emergency hold, run scheduled combined kernel+driver upgrades in a controlled window, and track exceptions.

Emma L: Agreed. Short-term: 72h emergency hold for eu-west and a rollback to 535.116 on canary. Medium-term: implement upgrade gating in the release pipeline + a compatibility matrix file in infra repo. I'll create INC-2026-0421 and an RFC for the lockstep matrix + gated rollout policy.

Mike T: I'll own the rollback bundle and the canary smoke tests. Priya will own the apt hold + node labels. I'll also add a smoke job that runs `ring_allreduce` and a tiny model run to the deploy pipeline.

Priya S: Applying holds now via ansible job ansible-playbook playbooks/pin-nvidia.yml targeting eu-west (rolling). Will post results when finished.

Emma L: After Priya confirms holds and Mike validates canary, we will coordinate a controlled upgrade plan for all regions. Please add any logs or failing node IDs here. Thx :thumbsup:

Mike T: Adding quick remediation checklist to the incident ticket:
- mark packages held (apt-mark/ansible)
- cordon/taint bad nodes
- rollback canary to 535.116 + CUDA 12.1 + NCCL 2.16.x
- run nccl-healthcheck + model smoke
- if canary green -> staged rollout with gating and auto-rollback
- publish postmortem + compatibility matrix

sre-oncall: Adding cost note: rolling back and holding will slightly increase maintenance load and delay kernel CVE installs. We'll schedule a security window after the lockstep upgrade is validated.

Emma L: I'll follow up with a short incident summary and assign owners. Priya: ping when ansible run completes. Mike: ping when canary smoke passes or fails.

(emoji reactions and followups will be logged in the incident ticket)
